item.title: New cyberviolence prevention grants support community-led initiatives
item.description:
New cyberviolence prevention grants support community-led initiatives jenniferdhogan Wed, 11/04/2026 - 15:15

Seven community organizations are receiving provincial funding from the new Cyberviolence Prevention Grant to help young Islanders build safer and more respectful online communities. 

Through the Interministerial Women's Secretariat, the province is investing $100,000 in community-led initiatives that will help young people develop the skills and confidence they need to navigate digital spaces safely. The initiative is a key action under Prince Edward Island's Youth Cyberviolence Prevention Strategy and will support projects designed to prevent cyberbullying, promote healthy online behaviour and increase awareness of cyberviolence among youth.

"Digital spaces are an important part of everyday life for young people, offering opportunities to learn, connect and express themselves. These community-led projects will help equip young Islanders with the knowledge and tools they need to stay safe online while fostering a culture of respect, inclusion and kindness in digital spaces."

- Minister of Workforce and Advanced Learning and Minister responsible for the Status of Women, Jenn Redmond.

The grant program was developed in response to feedback gathered during consultations for the Youth Cyberviolence Prevention Strategy. Young people, parents, caregivers and community partners identified the need for stronger support, practical resources and greater awareness to address cyberviolence and its impacts.

More than half of parents and caregivers surveyed during the strategy's development reported that a young person in their care had experienced some form of cyberviolence. Funded projects include cyberbullying prevention, digital citizenship education, youth leadership development, and resources tailored to newcomer youth, LGBTQIA+ youth, and young people with learning disabilities. 

“With this grant, STEAM PEI and the PEI IT Alliance are working together hosting Cyber Titans, a program to empower young Islanders with the knowledge, skills, and confidence they need to thrive in an increasingly digital world,” said STEAM PEI director of partnership and development Emily Wood. “These learning opportunities will promote healthy online behaviours by allowing youth to develop the skills to recognize online vulnerabilities, understand the impact of their digital interactions, and make informed choices that contribute to safer, more respectful, and inclusive online communities across the Island.”

For more information on the Provincial Youth Cyberviolence Prevent Strategy and resources on cyber safety, visit cybersafecarepei.ca. 

 

Media contact:
April Gallant
Department of Workforce and Advanced Learning
aldgallant@gov.pe.ca

 

Backgrounder: 

Cyberviolence Prevention Grant Recipients 2026

Learning Disabilities Association of PEI; for their project: Cyber Violence Prevention for those with Learning Disabilities, a project that will enhance awareness, education, and action toward preventing cyberviolence in Prince Edward Island by delivering targeted, accessible training and resources focused on youth with learning disabilities.

Amount: $8,000

Chinese Society of PEI: for their project, Safe Screens PEI: Chinese Youth Against Cyberviolence; a six-month bilingual prevention project for Chinese, immigrant, racialized and linguistically diverse youth in PEI, with priority for girls and young women.

Amount: $10,000

PEERS Alliance; for their project: Building Resillience: An Anti Cyber violence campaign, where workshops will be developed for various demographics within the LGBTQIA+ Demographic and be presented to various focus groups with both organizations and community members to gain a broader understanding of the specific kinds of rhetoric individuals are being subjected to.

Amount: $15,000

Sport PEI: for their project; Play with Respect. Post with Respect, where SPORT PEI will create a province-wide awareness campaign and host Community Engagement Activations promoting positive digital cultures and encourage respectful online behavior. The project will also develop a Digital Playbook, providing tips on communication best practices, platform guidance, sample templates, reporting information and educational resources for athletes, coaches, officials, volunteers and families.

Amount: $15,000

Community Legal Information Association of Prince Edward Island: for their project Earlier Education, Stronger Prevention: Expanding Cyberbullying Intervention; a project that will create an interactive, trauma-informed, and age-appropriate educational resource for PEI youth aged 10-11 and deliver the pilot workshop meeting the Health & Phys Ed. curriculum outcomes for grades 5-6.

Amount: $17,250

East Prince Women’s Information Centre (EPWIC): for their project, Youth Creating Healthy Digital Spaces & Culture, where EPWIC and Generation XX will create a Youth Digital Leadership Team and Speakers Bureau in response to PEI’s Provincial Youth Cyberviolence Prevention Strategy.

Amount: $17,250

S.T.E.A.M. PEI: for their project, Cyber Titans. Cyber Titans in partnership with the PEI IT Alliance which will empower PEI youth to prevent cyberviolence by building the knowledge, skills, and ethical foundation needed to become responsible digital citizens. The program combines hands-on cybersecurity training with education on cyber ethics, online safety, cyberbullying, harassment, image-based abuse, and the consequences of harmful online behaviour.

Amount: $17,500

item.title: Using nature to help protect the Victoria Causeway
item.description:
Using nature to help protect the Victoria Causeway jenniferdhogan Wed, 11/04/2026 - 11:04

Sometimes the best solutions to nature's challenges come from nature itself.

This past summer, members of the South Shore Watershed Association (SSWA) took on a project in collaboration with the PEI government to help slow erosion and reduce impacts to the Victoria causeway by using nature-based solutions.

Romy Munkres, project leader with SSWA, explained that the provincially-owned property next to the Victoria causeway roadway is eroding quickly.  

“This project location was chosen due to the high vulnerability of this section of coast, the proximity of the Victoria causeway road, and the government ownership of two parcels of land between the shoreline and the roadway,” Munkres says. 

“The Victoria causeway is one of the most erosion-prone on the south shore and the road is very important as it is one of only two routes providing access to the village of Victoria-by-the-Sea.”

The project uses a nature-based approach with many benefits. Native salt-tolerant shrubs will be planted along the bank and their roots will gradually stabilize the soil over the coming years to help slow erosion.

“We are planting throughout the 15-meter buffer zone to create a web of roots that will grow further inland over time,” they said. “The nature-based solution uses native plants that will not negatively impact the area and reduce erosion, while maintaining the area’s natural habitat.”

For this location, wild rose and bayberry were used. Munkres explained they were useful for several reasons.

“First, these shrubs are incredibly tolerant of salt, which is vital in a coastal planting site. Second, they have deep roots to help to stabilize the soil and hold the bank together, slowing erosion. Third, they are native species to the island. Using native species in nature-based solutions is important because they are perfectly adapted to local conditions and can do the job that they are being used for. In this case, they help stabilize an eroding cliff.”

Long term, the hope is that this planting will spread throughout the buffer zone and beyond, creating a stable web of roots that holds the loose, sandy soil together and slows erosion along the bank. 

“Erosion is a natural process and there is no solution, nature-based or engineered, that will hold erosion back forever, so the idea is to slow the erosion from reaching the causeway road and increase the lifespan of the road,” Munkres said.

Brian Thompson, Director of the Department's Land and Environment Division, says projects of this nature have been very successful thanks to partnerships between provincial government and watershed groups across the province. 

“The experience and efforts of the South Shore Watershed Association are greatly appreciated,” he says. “The partnerships we have developed with local watershed groups have been instrumental in moving these projects forward.”

With a nature-based approach, the benefits are far reaching. Besides being more cost effective, it also causes less interference to the habitat and the native species that live there.

“This location is home to a flourishing colony of bank swallows, a threatened species, and a well-used beach,” they added. “Nature-based solutions were the best option to reduce erosion and protect both the swallows and the beach.”

SSWA and the provincial government recognize that more actions may be needed in the future to ensure the causeway continues to protect this important infrastructure.

For now, the preferred option is the nature-based approach.

item.title: Premier McLeod on the Enbridge Line 21 Pipeline
item.description:
YELLOWKNIFE - Premier Bob McLeod issued the following statement on the Enbridge Line 21 pipeline today:

“I was pleased to learn that operations have resumed for Enbridge’s Line 21 pipeline after almost 2 years of no activity.

"Resource development has, and will continue to be, the backbone of our economy and is central to ensuring a good source of middle class jobs and business opportunities. Our territory has mineral and petroleum resources and the development of those resources can have a transformative effect on our people and economy.

"Sustainable economic development is key to the future of Northerners. With a strong resource development base, we will be able to support diversification of our local economies into emerging and established sectors.

"On behalf of the Government of the Northwest Territories I’d like to offer my congratulations to Imperial Oil, Enbridge the town of Norman Wells and other partners for getting this pipeline back up and running. I know the efforts and economic impacts of the pipeline have already begun to take shape in the community and will be felt for years to come. ”

 

Charlotte Digness
Media and Communications Coordinator
Cabinet Communications and Protocol
Government of the Northwest Territories
